spots.name: Ducal Castle
spots.summary: The Ducal Castle, also known as the Castle of the Dukes of Pomerania, and the Szczecin Castle, is a renaissance castle in the city of Szczecin, Poland, located at the Castle Hill in the Stare Miasto neighbourhood, near the Oder river. It is built in the gothic and Pomeranian mannerism architectural style.

spots.name: Szczecin Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The St. James the Apostle Archcathedral Basilica is a Gothic cathedral located in Szczecin, Poland and seat of the Archdiocese of Szczecin-Kamień.

names.zh: 什切青宗徒雅各伯圣殿主教座堂

spots.name: Hay Market Square

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Hay Market Square is an urban square in Szczecin, Poland. It is located between Sienna and Księcia Mściwoja II Streets, within the Old Town neighbourhood of the Downtown district. It was developed in the Middle Ages as a market place. One of buildings neighbouring it is the Old Town Hall, dating to the 15th century.

spots.name: Szczecin Terrases
spots.summary: Bolesław I the Brave Embankment, also known as Haken Terrace, is an observation deck in Szczecin, Poland. Located on an escarpment along the Oder river, it is 500 metres long and, together with the National Museum, Ducal Castle, and Cathedral Basilica of St. James the Apostle, it forms an urban and architectural plan.

spots.name: National Museum in Szczecin

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The National Museum in Szczecin is a national museum in Szczecin, Poland, established on 1 August 1945. The museum features ancient and modern art, archaeological, historical, numismatic, nautical and ethnographic collections and is divided into six branches, five located in Szczecin and one in Gryfice.

spots.name: Grunwald Square
spots.summary: The Grunwald Square is a circular urban square in Szczecin, Poland, within the Centre neighbourhood in the Downtown district. It forms a roundabout at the intersection of Pope John Paul II Avenue, Piłsudski Street, Rayski Street, and Śląska Street.

spots.name: Harbour Gate
spots.summary: The Harbour Gate, formerly known as the Berlin Gate, and the Brandenburg Gate, is a historic Baroque city gate in Szczecin, Poland, located at the intersection of Independence Avenue, Wyszyńskiego Street, and Victory Square.

spots.name: Old Town Hall
spots.summary: The Old Town Hall is a historic Gothic and Baroque town hall building in Szczecin, Poland. It is located at 8 Księcia Mściwoja II Street, next to the Hay Market Square and the New Market Square, within the Old Town neighbourhood of the Downtown district.

spots.name: Monument to Polish Endeavor
spots.summary: The Monument to the Polish Endeavour, also known as the Three Eagles Monument, and the Eagles' Nest, is a monument in the city of Szczecin, Poland, located at the Bright Meadows Square, at the boundary with the Jan Kasprowicz Park. It was designed by Gustaw Zemła, and unveiled in 1979.

spots.name: Hanza Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Hanza Tower is a skyscraper in Szczecin, Poland, located at the 50 Wyzwolenia Avenue, in the Śródmieście-Północ municipal neighbourhood. The building is 125 m tall, making it the tallest building in the city. It has 34 floors, including 4 underground. Its construction begun in 2011, and had been finished in 2021.

spots.name: King's Gate
spots.summary: The King's Gate, formerly known as the Anklam Gate, and sometimes also referred to as the Prussian Homage Gate, is a historic Baroque city gate in Szczecin, Poland, located at the Prussian Homage Square, at the intersection of Matejki Street and Polish Soldier Square.

spots.name: Szczecin Philharmonic
spots.summary: Szczecin Philharmonic, officially Mieczysław Karłowicz Philharmonic, founded in 1948, is a philharmonic of the city of Szczecin, Poland. In 2015, the new building of the philharmonic was awarded the European Union Prize for Contemporary Architecture.

spots.name: Emerald Lake
spots.summary: Lake, artificial cave and forest area (Puszcza Bukowa) situated in Zdroje district. Many great views on the city and nice area for hiking and bike riding.

spots.name: Red Town Hall
spots.summary: The Red Town Hall, also known as the New Town Hall, is a historic Gothic Revival town hall building in Szczecin, Poland. It is placed at 4 Stephen Báthory Square, within the New Town neighbourhood of the Downtown district. It was designed by Konrad Kruhl, and opened in 1897, as the seat of municipal government.

names.fr: Nouvel hôtel de ville de Szczecin

spots.name: Rodło Square
spots.summary: The Rodło Square is an urban square in Szczecin, Poland. It is located in the neighbourhood of Centre, within the Downtown district, at the intersection of Emancipation Avenue and Piłsudskiego Street. It was constructed in the 1970s.

spots.name: Szczecin Voivodeship Office
spots.summary: West Pomeranian Voivodeship Office Building is a historic administrative building, opened in 1911 and located at the Chrobry Embankment in the city of Szczecin, Poland.

names.fr: Bâtiment de la préfecture voévodale à Szczecin

spots.name: Różanka Rose Garden
spots.summary: The Różanka Rose Garden, is a two-hectare botanical garden in the Łękno area of Szczecin, Poland.

spots.name: Colleoni Monument in Szczecin
spots.summary: The equestrian statue of Bartolomeo Colleoni is a bronze equestrian statue in Szczecin, Poland, placed at the Aviators Square, within the neighbourhood of Centrum. It is dedicate to Bartolomeo Colleoni, a 15-century mercenary and a captain general in service of the Republic of Venice.

spots.name: Castle Route
spots.summary: Piotr Zaremba Castle Route is an overpass road in Szczecin, Poland, that is a part of the Voivodeship Road 115. It is one of 4 main roads of Szczecin, connecting the city and Police County with the rest of Poland.

spots.name: White Eagle Square
spots.summary: The White Eagle Square, prior to 1945 known as the Horse Market Square, is an urban square in Szczecin, Poland, within the Old Town neighbourhood of the Downtown district. It is located between Koński Kierat, Bogdanki, Grodzka, and Staromłyńska Streets.

spots.name: Jana Pawła II Avenue
spots.summary: Pope John Paul II Avenue, also commonly referred to as the Fountain Avenue is an avenue located in the areas of the Centrum and Śródmieście-Północ neighborhoods in the Śródmieście district of Szczecin.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Pope John Paul II Avenue, Szczecin

spots.name: Piłsudskiego Street
spots.summary: Józef Piłsudski Street is located in Centrum, Szczecin, within the Śródmieście district. The street spans approximately 926 m and runs roughly from east to west, connecting Jan Matejko Street with Gray Ranks Square.

spots.summary: The Pomeranian Landowners Palace, also known as the General Landscape Administration of Pomerania Building, is a historical Baroque Revival palace in Szczecin, Poland, located at 40 Independence Avenue in the neighbourhood of Centrum.

spots.summary: The Sts. Peter and St. Paul Church is a Brick Gothic Polish Old Catholic parish church in Szczecin, Poland, within the Downtown district. It is placed at 4 and 5 Sts. Peter and Paul Square, at the corner of Castle Route and Tadeusz Mazowiecki Street, within the neighbourhood of Old Town.

spots.name: Polish Soldier Square
spots.summary: The Polish Soldier Square, also commonly referred to as the Flower Avenue, is an urban square in Szczecin, Poland, located at the bounry of neighbourhoods of Centrum and Old Town, within the Downtown district.

spots.name: Maiden Tower
spots.summary: The Maiden Tower, also known as the Tower of Seven Coats, is a historic Gothic defensive tower in Szczecin, Poland. It is located at 47 Panieńska Street in the administrative neighbourhood of the Old Town. It was constructed in the 15th century, sometime before 1462, as part of the city fortifications.

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The building where two rulers of Russia (Catherine II and Maria Fiodorovna) were born.

spots.name: Hercules Fighting with a Centaur
spots.summary: Hercules Fighting with a Centaur, also known as The Fight of a Lapith with a Centaur, is a 1916 sandstone sculpture by Ludwig Manzel, displayed in Szczecin, Poland, within the neighbourhood of Old Town. It is placed at the Bolesław I the Brave Embankment in front of the Main Building of Szczecin National Museum.

spots.name: The Fiery Birds
spots.summary: The Fiery Birds is a modernist steel sculpture in Szczecin, Poland, placed in the Kasprowicz Park, depicting eighteen colourful birds. It was designed by Władysław Hasior, and originally unveiled in 1975 next to the Ducal Castle. In 1980, it was moved to the Concord Square, and again, in 1994, to its current location.

spots.name: Independence Avenue
spots.summary: Independence Avenue is an avenue street in Szczecin, Poland, located in the Downtown district, crossing the neighbourhoods of Centre and New Town. It is placed on north–south axis.

spots.name: Statue of Flora
spots.summary: The statue of Flora is a sandstone sculpture in Szczecin, Poland, placed at the White Eagle Square. It consists of a statue of Flora, goddess of flowers and spring in Roman mythology, with two putti standing next to her legs, one with a flower basket, and one with a cornucopia.

spots.name: Aviators Square
spots.summary: The Aviators Square, until 1945 known as the Augusta Square, is an urban square in Szczecin, Poland, located in the neighbourhood of Centre within the Downtown district.

spots.name: Statue of the Sailor
spots.summary: The statue of the Sailor is a sculpture in Szczecin, Poland, within the Centre neighbourhood of the Downtown district. It is placed on the Pope John Paul II Avenue, next to the Grunwald Square. The statue was designed by Ryszard Chachulski and unveiled on 19 June 1980.

spots.name: Statue of King Matt the First
spots.summary: The statue of King Matt the First is a monument in Szczecin, Poland, placed in front of the 54th Primary School, at 9 Rayskiego Street. It is dedicated to writer Janusz Korczak and consists of a statue depicting the titular character from his 1923 children's novel King Matt the First.

spots.name: Pomeranian Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Pomeranian Library, in full Stanisław Staszic Pomeranian Library is a Regional Library based in Szczecin, Poland. It is the largest humanities oriented library in West Pomerania, with a focus on social sciences, Pomeranian, Scandinavian and German subjects and Seamanship.

spots.name: December 1970 Monument in Szczecin
spots.summary: The Memorial to the Victims of December 1970, also colloquially known as the Angel of Freedom, is a monument in Szczecin, Poland, placed at the Solidarity Square, within the Old Town neighbourhood. The monument is dedicated to the victims of the suppression of December 1970 protests in Szczecin.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Memorial to the Victims of December 1970

spots.name: Kurkowa Street
spots.summary: Interesting tenement near the Old Town. Go from Old Town in direction of Castle, and you'll see it after about 20–30 m on the left side. It is painted flashy orange, you can't miss it.

spots.name: Jan Kasprowicz Park
spots.summary: The Jan Kasprowicz Park, also known as the Kasprowicz Park, and until 1945 known as Quistorp Park, is the biggest urban park in Szczecin, Poland located within municipal neighbourhood of Łękno near the boundaries of Śródmieście–Północ and Niebuszewo–Bolinko. The area of the park is circa 27.03 ha.

spots.name: Amphitrite Fountain
spots.summary: The Amphitrite Fountain, also known as the statue of Amphitrite, and the Felderhoff Fountain, was a Baroque Revival fountain sculpture in the city of Szczecin, Poland, placed at the intersection of current Independence Avenue, Wyszyńskiego Street, and the Victory Square, in front of the Harbour Gate.

spots.name: Palace of the Heads

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palace of the Heads is a historical neoclassical building in Szczecin, Poland, located at 1 Staromłyńska Street and 2 Polish Soldier Square, in the Old Town neighbourhood. It consists of two conjoined tenements, dating to the 18th century.
